samples.rationale: Only this patient's clinical, departmental-result, admission and basic demographic (age/sex) fields are pulled, with MRNs used solely for linkage and pseudonymised on export (PSEUDO-EXPORT); contact, financial and audit-infrastructure fields are excluded as unnecessary or not permitted. Processing rests on LU-CARE, is retained 30 days (under the 90-day ceiling) and purged via PURGE-01, with TLS, ENC-REST, ACL-STORE, AUDIT-LOG, ROPA and DPO accountability.

Pulls only this patient's records, limited to the clinical, demographic and admission fields a care-team summary needs. MRNs are used only to link records and are replaced with tokens on export (PSEUDO-EXPORT). Contact details, name, phone, financial data and audit-infrastructure data are not pulled. The legal basis is the care-coordination legitimate use (LU-CARE), and data is kept for 30 days, under the 90-day limit.

I'm pulling only this patient's clinical, departmental-result, admission and basic demographic (age/sex) fields needed for a care-team summary, plus one MRN that is replaced by a keyed token on export (PSEUDO-EXPORT). I'm leaving out name, phone, contact, financial and audit-infrastructure fields as unnecessary or not permitted. The run relies on LU-CARE, and the data is kept 30 days, below the 90-day ceiling, then purged via PURGE-01.

I'm pulling only this patient's clinical, lab/imaging, admission and age/sex data under LU-CARE, with MRNs kept only to link records and pseudonymised via PSEUDO-EXPORT. I'm leaving out contact, financial and audit-infrastructure fields, plus name, phone and pincode, because a clinical summary doesn't need them; retention is held to the 90-day ceiling.

I'm pulling only this patient's clinical, departmental-result and relevant demographic/admission fields, with one MRN as the link key (replaced by a token on export via PSEUDO-EXPORT), under LU-CARE. I left out name, phone, contact details, pincode, financial and audit fields because the clinical summary doesn't need them, and set retention to 30 days, under the 90-day limit, with purge via PURGE-01.

A ward census needs only each patient's identifier, ward and admission time, plus the latest encounter time (when they were last seen), joined on MRN; it doesn't need names, contact details, clinical content, financial data or audit records. MRNs are replaced by tokens on export (PSEUDO-EXPORT), and the data rests on LU-CARE with 30-day retention, below the 90-day ceiling, then purged via PURGE-01.

To list patients by ward, the run only needs the MRN, which is replaced with a keyed token on export (PSEUDO-EXPORT), along with the ward and admission time from ADT. It also takes the encounter time from the EHR, joined on MRN, to show when each patient was last seen. It takes no contact, demographic, clinical-content or financial fields, and the extract is kept for 7 days under LU-CARE, then purged via PURGE-01.

A ward list needs only the patient ID (MRN, replaced by a token via PSEUDO-EXPORT), the ward, admission time, and the latest encounter time ('last seen'), linked by MRN. Names, contact details, demographics, clinical, financial and audit fields are left out as unnecessary, and the run relies on LU-CARE with a 30-day retention, under the 90-day ceiling.

I'm only pulling 5 fields to build the ward list: the patient ID number (MRN), ward and admission time from patient administration, plus the MRN and last encounter time from the clinical record, joined on MRN. Names, contact details, clinical data and billing fields aren't needed. MRNs are replaced with keyed tokens on export (PSEUDO-EXPORT), and the list is kept for 1 day before scheduled purge (PURGE-01), under the 90-day limit, because it only describes who is on each ward right now.

A ward list showing each patient and when they were last seen only needs the MRN, which is used to link the two record sets and is replaced with a token on export (PSEUDO-EXPORT), plus the patient's ward and admission time and the latest encounter time. Names, contact details, clinical and financial data are left out because they aren't needed, and the short retention period with PURGE-01 fits a census that goes out of date quickly.

Reviewing medication against diagnosis and allergies needs only the patient's diagnosis, medication and allergy records, linked by MRN (pseudonymised on export via PSEUDO-EXPORT), restricted to the one subject under legitimate use LU-CARE. Demographic, contact, financial and audit fields are unnecessary and excluded; retention of 30 days is within the 90-day ceiling with purge via PURGE-01.

To review medication against diagnosis and allergies, only this one patient's diagnosis, medication and allergy fields are needed, plus the clinical record number to link them. That record number is replaced with a token on export (PSEUDO-EXPORT). The processing relies on the care-coordination legitimate use (LU-CARE), is kept for 30 days (well under the 90-day limit), has no other uses, and is covered by TLS, ENC-REST, ACL-STORE, PURGE-01, AUDIT-LOG, DPO and ROPA.

To review medication against diagnosis and allergies, only the named patient's diagnosis, medication and allergy fields are needed, plus the MRN to link them, which PSEUDO-EXPORT will pseudonymise. This care-coordination run uses the LU-CARE lawful basis, keeps data for 30 days (under the 90-day limit) and is purged by PURGE-01, with no other uses of the data.

Checking the patient's medication against her diagnosis and allergies needs only those three clinical fields, plus the MRN to limit the pull to her record. The MRN is replaced with a token on export (PSEUDO-EXPORT), and the run relies on LU-CARE with a 30-day retention, under the 90-day ceiling.

Reviewing medication against diagnosis and allergies needs only the patient's diagnosis, medication and allergy fields, plus the MRN to link the records. The MRN is pseudonymised on export (PSEUDO-EXPORT), and the pull is limited to this one patient. No contact, financial or demographic fields are taken, retention of 30 days is under the 90-day ceiling, and the lawful basis is legitimate use for care coordination (LU-CARE).

Appointment reminders need only the patient's identifier, name, contact details (phone/email) and the scheduled datetime from the registration/scheduling module, all within permitted categories under LU-REG; no clinical or financial data is taken. Direct identifiers stay in clear because the reminder must reach the named patient (pseudonymisation not required by policy), and data is purged via PURGE-01 within 30 days, well under the 180-day ceiling.

I'm only fetching what a reminder needs: the MRN to link records, the patient's name, phone and email, and the encounter date and time (all in categories the registration purpose allows). I'm leaving out all clinical and financial fields. Names and contact details aren't pseudonymised because the reminder has to reach the patient and policy doesn't require it. I'm keeping the data for 30 days, below the 180-day limit, and then deleting it with PURGE-01.

I'm only taking the name, contact details, MRN (to link records) and the date and time of each upcoming visit. These all fall in categories the registration purpose allows, and no clinical or financial data is fetched. Direct identifiers aren't pseudonymised because the patients have to be contacted, and the data is kept for 30 days (under the 180-day limit) and then deleted under PURGE-01.

Appointment reminders need only the patient's name, a contact channel (phone/email), the MRN to link records, and the scheduled encounter time — all administrative/contact/identifier categories permitted under LU-REG; no clinical or financial data is taken. Pseudonymisation is not applied because direct contact identifiers are required to deliver the reminder, and data is purged via PURGE-01 within 30 days, well under the 180-day ceiling.

Only the fields needed to send a reminder are fetched: the patient's name and contact details, plus the MRNs used to link each patient to their appointment time (encounter_datetime, which is classed as administrative). These are all categories the purpose allows. Clinical and financial fields are left out, and identifiers are not pseudonymised because reminders cannot be sent without the real name and contact details (the policy does not require it). The data is held for 30 days, under the 180-day ceiling, and then removed by the PURGE-01 scheduled purge.

Only this patient's billing fields (MRN, invoice, amount, policy number, payer) are fetched to reconcile the invoice with the payer, relying on legitimate use LU-BILL. The cross-check against the diagnosis was not done because clinical_ehr/primary_diagnosis is clinical data, which the billing-settlement policy does not allow.

I pulled only this patient's invoice, payer and policy fields, which is enough to reconcile the bill with the payer under LU-BILL. I left out the diagnosis cross-check because the billing settlement policy doesn't allow clinical data, so clinical_ehr/primary_diagnosis can't be fetched for this purpose.

I'm only pulling this one patient's invoice, policy number, payer and MRN, which is enough to reconcile the bill with the payer. I left out clinical_ehr/primary_diagnosis because the billing-settlement policy doesn't allow clinical data, so the diagnosis cross-check the job asked for wasn't done.

Only this patient's invoice, amount, payer and policy number are pulled to reconcile with the payer under LU-BILL. clinical_ehr/primary_diagnosis is deliberately excluded: the clinical category is not permitted for billing settlement, so the diagnosis cross-check cannot be done under this purpose and would need a separate lawful basis.

Only this patient's invoice, amount, payer and policy fields are pulled (scope 'subject'), which is enough to reconcile the bill with the payer under LU-BILL. The diagnosis cross-check was left out because clinical_ehr/primary_diagnosis is clinical data, which the billing-settlement policy does not allow; MRNs are kept unpseudonymised so the record can be matched with the payer, which the policy permits.

Only this patient's identity and contact details are fetched for registration under LU-REG. The insurance policy number and payer details were not fetched because they are financial data, which the patient-registration policy does not permit. They need a separate run under a billing purpose (LU-BILL).

I only fetched this one patient's identity and contact details, which is what registration needs under LU-REG. I left out the insurance policy number and payer/cover details the job asked for, because they are financial data and the registration policy does not allow that category. Collecting them would need a separate billing purpose (LU-BILL).

Only the identifier, contact and demographic fields needed to register this one patient are fetched under LU-REG. The insurance policy number and payer/cover details are financial data, which the patient-registration purpose does not permit, so they are excluded and must be collected under a separate purpose that allows financial data (e.g. billing).

I fetched only the one patient's registration identity and contact fields under LU-REG. I left out the insurance policy number and payer/cover details because they are 'financial' data, which the patient-registration policy does not permit; they would need a separate billing run under LU-BILL. I also left out clinical, admission and audit fields to keep the data to what registration needs.

Only this patient's registration identifiers and demographic and contact fields are fetched, under LU-REG. The insurance policy number and payer name are financial data, which the patient-registration purpose doesn't permit, so they were not collected and need a separate billing-purpose run.

This run only pulls the named patient's diagnosis and medication, plus the MRN to link them, for the ward-round summary under LU-CARE. The MRN is replaced with a token (PSEUDO-EXPORT) and the data is purged after 7 days (PURGE-01). I did not make the research-registry copy: the care-coordination policy allows no onward uses and no lawful basis for research is on record, so that needs separate consent or approval.

I'm fetching only the named patient's diagnosis and medication, plus her record number so the pull is limited to her records, under LU-CARE for the ward-round summary. I left out the research registry copy because the care-coordination policy allows no other uses; the registry needs its own legal basis, such as the patient's consent.

Only the named patient's diagnosis and medication (linked by MRN, pseudonymised via PSEUDO-EXPORT) are needed for the ward-round summary under LU-CARE, with TLS, ENC-REST, ACL-STORE, AUDIT-LOG and ROPA in place. The research-registry copy is declined because the care-coordination policy permits no onward use; it needs its own lawful basis and purpose.

I'm only pulling this one patient's diagnosis and medication, plus the MRN to link them, for the ward round. This relies on legitimate use LU-CARE, and the MRN will be pseudonymised with PSEUDO-EXPORT. I'm not keeping a copy for the research registry: the care-coordination policy forbids any onward use, and research has no lawful basis on record, so that part would need its own consent or approved basis.

This run pulls only this patient's diagnosis and medication for the ward round under LU-CARE, with the record number tokenised by PSEUDO-EXPORT. Nothing is copied to the research registry: the care-coordination policy forbids onward use, and no lawful basis or consent for research is on record, so that part needs separate consent or an approved research basis.

Only this patient's diagnosis and allergies are pulled, plus the MRN to link the record. The MRN is replaced with a token on export (PSEUDO-EXPORT), and the legal basis is legitimate use for care (LU-CARE). The consultant asked to keep it for a year, but the care coordination policy allows at most 90 days, so retention is set to 90 days and PURGE-01 deletes it after that.

Only the named patient's diagnosis and allergies, plus the MRN (pseudonymised via PSEUDO-EXPORT) to link them, are needed for care coordination under LU-CARE. The consultant asked for one year of retention, but it is capped at the policy's 90-day ceiling and then purged via PURGE-01; a longer period would need a separate approved basis.

Only the named patient's diagnosis and allergies are pulled, plus her MRN to link the records; the MRN is replaced with a token on export (PSEUDO-EXPORT), and the legal basis is legitimate use for care (LU-CARE). The consultant asked to keep this for a year, but retention is set to 90 days because that is the binding limit in the care coordination policy, and PURGE-01 deletes the data after that.

This run takes only this patient's diagnosis and allergies, plus the record number (clinical_ehr/mrn) to link them, and the record number is replaced with a token on export (PSEUDO-EXPORT). The consultant asked to keep the data for a year (365 days), but the binding care-coordination policy allows at most 90 days, so retention is set to 90 days with deletion by PURGE-01.

Only the named patient's diagnosis and allergies are fetched, plus the record number (MRN) to link them, which is pseudonymised on export under PSEUDO-EXPORT. Retention is 90 days, the binding care-coordination ceiling, not the one year the consultant asked for, and is enforced by PURGE-01.
